quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 22

questions.question: A yellow traffic light warns that it will turn red soon. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Continue and safely clear the intersection.
Speed up to avoid an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue and safely clear the intersection.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, drive through safely to clear the intersection as quickly as possible.

questions.question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change as speed increases?

options.text: They decrease.
They stay the same.
They increase.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds cause longer stopping distances and more severe crashes. As speed increases, the chance of serious injury or death also increases. Leave more space between your vehicle and the one ahead when you drive faster.

questions.question: You should keep your signal on while turning because it:

options.text: Is required by law throughout the entire turn.
Tells other drivers what you plan to do.
Makes turning safer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This tells other drivers, riders, and pedestrians your intentions.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, you should:

options.text: Brake hard.
Keep the same speed.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the same speed.
questions.explanation: When being passed, maintain your speed and do not speed up. Let the other vehicle pass safely and merge back into your lane.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Change lanes inside an intersection.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
Watch for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes inside an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes inside an intersection. Always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Watch for other drivers in the lane you want to enter.

questions.question: A broken yellow line between two lanes means:

options.text: Both lanes go in the same direction.
You can pass when it is safe.
You cannot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions. You can pass when there is no oncoming traffic in the passing lane.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Anything that makes you swerve while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind off the road. It is a major cause of traffic crashes. Distractions prevent you from noticing dangers and other vehicles.

questions.question: Backing your vehicle is:

options.text: Always dangerous.
Dangerous only if you have a helper.
Dangerous only in large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always dangerous.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see well behind your vehicle. Always back up slowly and carefully.

questions.question: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with lights on, you should:

options.text: Stop and ask if emergency workers need help.
Speed up to pass the scene quickly.
Move to the farthest lane away or slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the farthest lane away or slow down.
questions.explanation: When approaching a stopped emergency vehicle with lights on, move to an available lane away from it. If you cannot move over, slow down to a safe speed and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Hydroplaning can happen at speeds as low as:

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when water sits on the road. Most tires can move water away at speeds up to 35 mph. Above 35 mph, tires cannot move water as well, and your tires may lose grip and slide like water skis.

questions.question: When can you cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle?

options.text: If the vehicle in front moves to the right.
If the yellow line on your side is broken.
If the yellow line on the opposite side is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the yellow line on your side is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means traffic on that side can pass if it is safe. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You can move back when you see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always check your blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.question: What does this sign on the back of a vehicle mean?

options.text: The vehicle is drawn by an animal.
The vehicle travels at 25 mph or slower.
The vehicle makes sudden stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle travels at 25 mph or slower.
questions.explanation: Slow-moving vehicles like bicycles, horse-drawn carts, and farm vehicles display this sign to warn drivers that they travel at 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: When parallel parking facing downhill, what should you do with your wheels?

options.text: Turn them sharply toward the side of the road.
Turn them away from the side of the road.
Keep them straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them sharply toward the side of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb or road edge. This prevents your vehicle from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving speed?

options.text: Driving too slowly is not unsafe.
Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speed does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly can frustrate other drivers and cause them to make dangerous passes. Drive with traffic flow at the legal speed limit.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: They disappear if you have one mirror on each side.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can check blind spots by looking in your rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have large blind spots that other drivers should avoid.

questions.question: If there is a deep puddle on the road ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Drive through it at normal speed.
Avoid it if possible.
Shift into neutral while driving through it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid it if possible.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery areas like deep puddles to prevent skidding. Dry, solid surfaces are safest for driving.

questions.question: What is the proper way to make a right turn?

options.text: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the center line.
Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb.
Approach from the right lane, then move toward the middle of the street before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb.
questions.explanation: Use your signal before turning. Slow down and stay as close as possible to the right curb or road edge when making a right turn.

questions.question: When is it legal to drive faster than the posted speed limit?

options.text: Never.
If you think it is reasonable and safe.
When you are passing another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Always obey the posted speed limit. You can drive slower based on road conditions, but never faster than the speed limit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Crossroad ahead.
Merge.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossroad ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is coming up ahead.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A flagger is ahead.
Turn left at the intersection.
Last turn before a toll road.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flagger is ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange is used for work zones. When you see orange signs, cones, or barrels, stay alert for unsafe driving conditions. This sign warns you that a flagger is ahead. You must follow the flagger's directions.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Stop completely, check for traffic, and go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, check for traffic, and go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road direction changes or narrows ahead.
No right turn.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road direction changes or narrows ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road direction changes or the road gets narrower. You may see these signs on sharp curves or near narrow bridges.

questions.question: You want to enter the freeway but see no gap in traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and force other drivers to make a gap.
Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap.
Stop at the end of the ramp to wait for a gap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap.
questions.explanation: If you do not see a gap, slow down on the ramp to wait. Do not stop at the end of the ramp. You need room to speed up to match traffic before entering the freeway.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the center line mean?

options.text: Reduce your speed.
A traffic light is ahead.
Do not pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. When there is a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line, the driver on the solid line side cannot pass. When both lines are solid, no one can pass from either direction.
